_comment: Maps COCO object labels (as returned by the EfficientDet-Lite0 model) to their primary chemical composition. 'primary' = elements that make up most of the mass / are essential to the object. 'trace' = present but minor. 'note' is a one-line explanation shown in the popup. Labels MUST match coco_labels.txt exactly (lowercase, multi-word with single spaces).

person.note: Human body: ~65% O, 18% C, 10% H by mass.

bicycle.note: Steel/aluminum frame, rubber tires (C, H), chain (Fe, Cr).

car.note: Steel body, aluminum engine, plastic interior, lithium/lead battery.

motorcycle.note: Similar materials to car at smaller scale.

bus.note: Heavy steel frame, aluminum panels, glass (Si, Na).

train.note: Steel rails and body, copper electrics.

boat.note: Aluminum/fiberglass hull, copper antifouling, bronze fittings.

traffic light.note: Aluminum housing; LEDs use GaN, GaP, InGaN.

stop sign.note: Aluminum sheet with reflective coating; pigments include Ti, Cr.

parking meter.note: Cast metal housing with electronics inside.

bench.note: Wood (cellulose: C, H, O) on iron supports — or fully recycled plastic.

bird.note: Same biological palette as humans; calcium-rich bones.

cat.note: Mammal body chemistry mirrors human composition.

dog.note: Mammal body chemistry mirrors human composition.

horse.note: Larger mammal — more calcium phosphate in skeleton.

sheep.note: Wool is keratin: lots of S in the disulfide bonds.

cow.note: Mammal — bones and milk are notably high in Ca.

elephant.note: Tusks are dentin: Ca, P, O dominant.

giraffe.note: Mammal — long bones, very high calcium content.

backpack.note: Nylon (C, H, N, O) and polyester fabrics with metal zippers.

handbag.note: Leather (collagen: C, H, N, O) often chromium-tanned, or PU plastic.

tie.note: Silk or polyester. Silk = fibroin protein (C, H, N, O, S).

suitcase.note: Polycarbonate or ABS shell on an aluminum frame.

frisbee.note: Polyethylene plastic — mostly C and H.

skis.note: Fiberglass and carbon-fiber composite over a wood core, metal edges.

sports ball.note: Vulcanized rubber (C, H, S) or leather. Air inside is N₂ + O₂.

kite.note: Ripstop nylon over carbon-fiber or aluminum spars.

baseball bat.note: Wooden bats: cellulose. Aluminum bats: Al alloy with Mg/Zn.

skateboard.note: Maple-wood deck, aluminum trucks, polyurethane wheels, steel bearings.

surfboard.note: Polyurethane/EPS foam core wrapped in fiberglass + epoxy.

tennis racket.note: Carbon-fiber frame with nylon or natural-gut strings.

bottle.note: PET plastic (C, H, O) or soda-lime glass (Si, O, Na, Ca).

wine glass.note: Soda-lime glass; some crystal still uses Pb.

cup.note: Ceramic (clay: Al, Si, O), porcelain, glass, or paper depending on cup.

bowl.note: Ceramic (kaolinite: Al, Si, O, H) or glass.

apple.note: ~85% water, sugars and fiber are C, H, O.

sandwich.note: Bread, protein, vegetables — biological C/H/O/N plus salt (Na, Cl).

broccoli.note: Sulfur-rich (sulforaphane) and high in iron and calcium.

hot dog.note: Processed meat in a wheat bun — biological C/H/O/N plus added sodium.

pizza.note: Wheat dough, cheese (calcium-rich), tomato, plus sodium.

donut.note: Flour, sugar, fat — almost pure C/H/O.

cake.note: Flour, sugar, eggs, dairy — sucrose is C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁.

chair.note: Wood, plastic, foam — varies; metal chairs are mostly Fe or Al.

couch.note: Wood frame, polyurethane foam, polyester or leather upholstery.

potted plant.note: Plants are cellulose (C, H, O); chlorophyll's center is Mg.

bed.note: Wood/metal frame, polyurethane foam mattress, cotton or polyester sheets.

dining table.note: Solid wood (cellulose), or MDF + veneer, often on metal legs.

toilet.note: Vitreous china — kaolin clay fired to a glassy ceramic.

tv.note: Silicon chips, indium-tin oxide screen, rare-earth phosphors (Y, Eu).

laptop.note: Silicon CPU, aluminum chassis, lithium-ion battery (Li, Co), neodymium speaker magnets.

mouse.note: ABS plastic shell, silicon chip, copper wires, optical sensor.

remote.note: Plastic case, silicon chip, alkaline (Zn, Mn) or lithium battery.

keyboard.note: ABS keys, silicon controller, copper traces, gold contacts.

cell phone.note: Silicon SoC, aluminum frame, Li-ion battery, indium-tin oxide touchscreen, rare earths in speakers and camera.

microwave.note: Steel cavity, magnetron contains barium-oxide cathode.

oven.note: Stainless steel body, ceramic insulation, nichrome (Ni, Cr) heating elements.

toaster.note: Stainless or chromed steel body, nichrome heating wire.

sink.note: Stainless steel basin (304 SS = 18% Cr, 8% Ni, rest Fe).

refrigerator.note: Steel cabinet, copper coils, polyurethane foam insulation, R-134a or R-600a refrigerant.

book.note: Cellulose paper, plus titanium-dioxide whiteners and carbon-black ink.

clock.note: Plastic case, silicon quartz oscillator, brass gears, alkaline battery.

scissors.note: Hardened stainless steel blades, plastic or rubber grips.

teddy bear.note: Polyester or cotton plush, polyester fiberfill stuffing.

hair drier.note: Plastic shell, copper-wound motor, nichrome heating element.

toothbrush.note: Polypropylene handle and nylon bristles — pure C/H/N polymers.
